items.q: The famous long odes of pre-Islamic Arabia, seven in the best-known collection.
The pre-Islamic poet whose Mu'allaqah opens "Qifa nabki", "Stop, let us weep".
The Arabic word for a long formal ode kept in one metre and one rhyme.
The Arabic word for a poet's collected poems.
The Arabic word for one line of verse, made of two halves.
The name of the rhyme that ends every line of a qasidah.
The science of the metres of Arabic poetry.
The scholar of Basrah who founded the science of Arabic metres.
items.a: al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩

items.q: The Companion known as the poet of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, who answered his enemies in verse.
The poem "Banat Su'ad" was recited before our Beloved Prophet ﷺ by this Companion poet.
The name usually given to al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ famous poem in praise of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The woman Companion poet famous for her elegies on her brother Sakhr.
The Egyptian poet given the title "Prince of Poets", who passed away in 1351 AH / 1932 CE.
The Abbasid poet who boasted "the horses, the night and the desert know me".
The knight of the tribe of 'Abs, born to an enslaved mother, whose ode is among the Mu'allaqat.
A poem of praise is called this in Arabic.
A poem mourning someone who has passed away is called this in Arabic.
Many old odes open by weeping over these, the traces of the beloved's abandoned camp.
The number of metres that al-Khalil ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ set down.
The market near Ta'if where the Arabs held yearly poetry contests before Islam.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ told this poet to answer the idolaters in verse, saying Jibril ﵇ was with him (meaning).
The pre-Islamic poet of wisdom whose Mu'allaqah praises two chiefs who made peace after the war of Dahis and al-Ghabra'.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ called the half-line "Indeed, everything apart from Allah is vain" the truest word a poet said. Whose line is it?
The youngest of the Mu'allaqat poets, said to have been killed in his twenties.
The poet of Taghlib whose Mu'allaqah of tribal pride opens "Ala hubbi bi-sahniki".
The two Umayyad poets who traded rival satires, called the Naqa'id, for about forty years.
The Christian poet of Taghlib at the Umayyad court, the third of the great Umayyad trio with Jarir and al-Farazdaq.
The Abbasid poet who compiled the anthology "Diwan al-Hamasah".
The pupil of Abu Tammam whose famous ode describes the ruined palace of Kisra.
The Abbasid poet best known for his poems on renouncing the world, the zuhdiyyat.
The Egyptian poet called "the Poet of the Nile".
The famous "Lamiyyat al-'Arab" is attributed to this outlaw poet of pre-Islamic Arabia.
items.src: Lamiyyat al-'Arab (some attribute it to Khalaf al-Ahmar)

items.q: The vizier-poet who wrote "Lamiyyat al-'Ajam".
The name for the outlaw poets of pre-Islamic Arabia, such as al-Shanfara and 'Urwah ibn al-Ward.
The Andalusian form of strophic poem with changing rhymes, often sung.
The poet of Cordoba famous for his Nuniyyah "Adha al-tana'i badilan min tadanina".
The letter that ends every line of al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ Burdah.
The scholar who wrote "al-Shi'r wa-l-Shu'ara'", a book on the poets and their poems.
The prince of Aleppo for whom al-Mutanabbi wrote many of his finest odes.
The ruler of Egypt whom al-Mutanabbi first praised and later satirised.
A poem of satire is called this in Arabic.
A poem of boasting about oneself or one's tribe is called this in Arabic.
The poet who wrote "Nations are only their morals while they last; if their morals go, they go".
The poet of the ode in which the Arabic language speaks: "I am the sea; pearls lie hidden in its depths".
The poet who wrote the elegy for his brother "Wa inna Sakhran la-ta'tammu al-hudatu bihi", likening him to a mountain with a fire on top.
The sixteenth metre, added by al-Akhfash al-Awsat ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ after al-Khalil.
The long metre of "Qifa nabki", built on fa'ulun mafa'ilun.
The metre of al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ Burdah and of "Banat Su'ad", built on mustaf'ilun fa'ilun.
The light metre of mustaf'ilun repeated, used for most teaching poems such as Ibn Malik's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ Alfiyyah.
The metre built on mutafa'ilun repeated, used in Labid's ﵁ Mu'allaqah.
The Kufan scholar who compiled the old anthology "al-Mufaddaliyyat".
The poet who judged other poets at Suq 'Ukaz from a red leather tent.
The pre-Islamic poet nicknamed "Sannajat al-'Arab" (the cymbal of the Arabs) for the music of his verse.
The Companion poet who was martyred at Mu'tah as the third commander of the army.
The Companion poet who was one of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk and whose repentance was accepted.
The imam of a school of fiqh to whom a well-known diwan of wisdom poetry is attributed.
items.src: Diwan al-Imam al-Shafi'i (attribution of some lines is doubtful)

items.q: Al-Busiri's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ second great poem in praise of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, rhyming in hamzah.
Ahmad Shawqi's poem in praise of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, written in the same metre and rhyme as al-Burdah.
Writing a poem in the same metre and rhyme as a famous one, to rival or honour it.
Adding three half-lines to every line of an older poem, so each verse has five parts.
Al-Mutanabbi's personal name and kunyah.
The vizier of Granada who wrote the muwashshah "Jadaka al-ghaythu".
The modern form that counts feet freely instead of keeping full lines, pioneered by Nazik al-Mala'ikah and Badr Shakir al-Sayyab.
The poet whose Mu'allaqah defends Bakr against Taghlib before King 'Amr ibn Hind.
Al-Khatib al-Tibrizi's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ commentary on the long odes covers this many poems.
Abu Tammam's anthology takes its name from its first and longest chapter, on this quality.
Abu Tammam's ode on the conquest of Amorium in 223 AH / 838 CE opens with this half-line (meaning).
items.a: The sword is truer than the books

items.q: The Sufi poet of Cairo called "Sultan al-'Ashiqin", author of the long Ta'iyyah.
Al-Shatibi's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ famous poem on the seven readings of the Qur'an, rhyming in lam.
Al-Laqqani's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ poem on Ash'ari creed.
The short poem on the terms of hadith science by al-Bayquni ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The beginners' poem on tajwid by Sulayman al-Jamzuri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
Ibn al-Jazari's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ poem on tajwid, learnt by heart by students of the Qur'an.
A teaching poem that sets out a whole science in verse, to be memorised.
The Maliki scholar Ibn al-Nahwi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ wrote the poem of hope that opens "Ishtaddi azmatu tanfariji". What is it called?
Arabic prosody names its building blocks after parts of a tent: the cord (sabab) and this.
A permitted small change in a metrical foot, such as dropping a quiet letter.
The outlaw poet whose nickname means "he carried evil under his arm".
The last great Bedouin poet of the Umayyad age, famous for his love of Mayy.
Chaste Bedouin love poetry, named after the tribe of Jamil Buthaynah.
The full title al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ gave his Burdah.
items.a: al-Kawakib al-Durriyyah fi Madh Khayr al-Bariyyah

items.q: The grammarian who wrote a well-known commentary on "Banat Su'ad".
The book by Ibn Sallam al-Jumahi that ranks the poets in classes.
Hassan ibn Thabit ﵁ is reported to have lived this long, half before Islam and half in Islam.
The name for poets whose lives spanned both the Jahiliyyah and Islam, such as Labid ﵁.
The biting satirist whom our master 'Umar ﵁ jailed for satirising al-Zibriqan ibn Badr.
The poet of Hudhayl whose 'Ayniyyah mourns his sons, who all passed away within one year.
The book on poetry and its criticism written by Ibn Rashiq of Qayrawan.
The early Abbasid writer whose "Naqd al-Shi'r" laid out rules for judging poems.
The Shafi'i scholar whose Lamiyyah of advice opens "I'tazil dhikra al-aghani wa-l-ghazal".
The poet of the Nuniyyah of wisdom that opens "Ziyadatu l-mar'i fi dunyahu nuqsanu".
The lexicographer whose poem rhyming in a short alif is called "al-Maqsurah".
The poet who mourned the fall of the cities of al-Andalus in the Nuniyyah "Li-kulli shay'in idha ma tamma nuqsanu".
The Andalusian nature poet nicknamed "al-Jannan", the gardener.
The Egyptian poet and statesman called "lord of the sword and the pen", who revived classical poetry and passed away in 1322 AH / 1904 CE.
The full title al-Busiri ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ gave his Hamziyyah.
items.a: Umm al-Qura fi Madh Khayr al-Wara

items.q: The rival satirists Jarir and al-Farazdaq both came from this great tribe of Najd.
The anthology of old poems compiled by al-Asma'i, a companion book to al-Mufaddaliyyat.
Ibn al-Farid's ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ long Sufi poem, also called "Nazm al-Suluk", rhymes in this letter.
The name for a line whose two halves both end in the rhyme, as in the opening line of most qasidahs.
Running a sentence on from one line into the next, which the old critics counted as a fault.
